The animal only nosed about the hole, and the pivotal initiative was the boys' own.' | '原子弹之父的审判 / The Trial of the Father of the Atomic Bomb' (p8) vs article p375: 'a security hearing, an administrative proceeding, not a criminal prosecution.' | '会算术的马 / The Horse That Could Count' (p3) vs article: 'The cues came from the questioners.' | '从车库到世界之巅 / From a Garage to the Top of the World' (p6) vs article p268: 'Apple's garage origins are largely symbolic; Wozniak calls their significance inflated.'
problem: Five chapter titles state as fact the popular myth that their own article explicitly debunks. Readers see the title first in the TOC and on the opener, then are told it is false. A teacher would read this as careless or self-contradictory, and it undercuts the preface's own promise: '一个广为流传的结论，证据是否充分？'
suggested_fix: Retitle ch13, ch56 and the English title of ch31. Treat ch07 and ch40 as optional. Ch13: '“卖掉”埃菲尔铁塔的骗子 / The Man Who “Sold” the Eiffel Tower' (or 'The Man Who Tried to Sell the Eiffel Tower Twice'). Ch56: '原子弹之父的安全听证会 / The Hearing That Ended Oppenheimer's Clearance'. Ch31 English: 'The Boys, the Dog and the Cave of Lascaux', keeping the Chinese. Change the TOC, opener, running footer and bookmarks together. The titles come from the owner-approved video scripts, so the owner must sign off.

Ch56 p375 says 'a security hearing, an administrative proceeding, not a criminal prosecution.' Ch31 p208 says 'The animal only nosed about the hole, and the pivotal initiative was the boys' own.' Web sources back the articles: Lustig's second mark went to the police before the deal closed (mentalfloss, awealthofcommonsense, fortune.com 'the man who tried to sell the Eiffel Tower twice'), and the AEC board itself said it worked 'in the spirit of inquiry, not that of a trial' (avalon.law.yale.edu opp01; ahf.nuclearmuseum.org). These three titles contradict their own articles. The ch07 and ch40 examples are weak. 'The Horse That Could Count' is the conventional name of the Clever Hans story, and the opener question ('汉斯是在算数，还是在读懂人的动作？') already frames it as a doubt. Ch40 only says the garage's significance is inflated, not that the garage story is false. The ch31 Chinese title (少年和一只狗) is defensible; only the English 'Found by a Dog' contradicts the text.

chapter: 全书 (Chinese translation pages, e.g. ch01)

evidence: Preface: '全书标注4017项重点词与短语'. The vocabulary lists actually contain 4,125 entries (4,063 distinct headword strings, counted from all 词汇与表达 pages); the project elsewhere says 3,500. suggested_fix: Generate the stated number from the built vocabulary list at build time and assert that it matches (as v5 does). Use '个' or '条'. If the cover keeps '考研重点词汇', optionally split the count into exam words and 专名/主题词.

The preface already says it '也收录理解故事所需的专名与主题词', so including proper names is disclosed and not an inflation. '项' is usable for counted items, though '个/条' is more natural. evidence: It opens with three rhetorical questions ('…为什么以为自己能够隐身？…如何从水族馆逃回大海？…为什么从“粗劣手艺”的证据变成研究线索？') and closes with three more ('证据是否充分？相关现象能否说明因果？…原来的解释还成立吗？'). It is the first prose a buyer reads and confirms the 'AI book' impression.
suggested_fix: Rewrite as a short, signed note in the author's own voice, with facts: why these 70 stories were chosen, who the book is for (考研英语一/二、四六级), how the videos and the book fit together, a suggested routine (e.g. read the English cold, check 词汇, then the translation and summary), and what the conventions mean. verify_reason: Every quoted phrase is on p2: three opening questions, three closing questions, '一个词怎样参与叙事，一个搭配怎样表达关系', '把词汇、句子与思考连在一起', '阅读也意味着追问', '多一份具体的内容，也多一份继续读下去的兴趣', and '在这里这样使用' followed by '在这里，'. The preface is unsigned and gives no usage or audience information. The diagnosis is accurate. The v5 rebuild already rewrote the preface at the owner's request, signed '朋克英语'.

evidence: The cover is one 1056×1500 px RGB raster (152 ppi at B5; chapter art is 260 ppi), with the title '考研学人', '70篇趣味英语阅读' and '科普 · 历史 · 趣闻 / 中英双语 · 考研重点词汇' baked into the image. The motif is an open book with a Mediterranean coast, Roman arch and paper ribbon spilling out of it. The ribbon carries sketches of the Colosseum, an armillary sphere and a toothed four-limbed fossil skeleton; no chapter is about fossils or armillary spheres. A Voyager-style probe flies through a daytime sky below the clouds, trailing a yellow streak. The triumphal arch's two piers do not match: the left has stacked engaged columns, the right a different column arrangement and a stray small opening.
problem: 'Landscape and objects bursting out of an open book', in glossy oversaturated watercolour, is one of the most recognisable AI-image clichés. The objects are a random collage rather than the book's stories, and the probe under the clouds is physically absurd. The baked-in lettering at 152 ppi will print soft with halo edges. The cover's display serif and navy/gold palette appear nowhere inside, where the design is a muted green sans layout, so the cover and interior look like two different products.
suggested_fix: Build the new cover around real chapter objects. The octopus, Roman concrete and the Golden Record probe already qualify; add more, such as the lemon, Penny Black, Tetris block and rice ear. Drop the unrelated fossil, armillary sphere and generic Mediterranean scenery. Set the cover text as live type, with art at ≥300 ppi CMYK plus bleed. Add the brand and video line.
verify_reason: The cover is a 1056×1500 RGB raster at 152 ppi (pdfimages). Page 1 has no live text, so the lettering is baked into the image. The open book spilling a landscape and the glossy watercolour are a common AI-image cliché. The fossil skeleton (an ichthyosaur-like marine reptile) and the armillary sphere match no chapter; the only fossil in the book is a leaf in ch21. One claim is inaccurate: the motifs are not purely random. The octopus (ch03), the Roman arch and Colosseum (ch14) and the Voyager-type probe (ch70) all match chapters. I could not confirm the arch-pier mismatch at this resolution, so I dropped it. The repo README already notes that only the 1056×1500 source exists.

chapter: 全书 (slash alternatives in translations and glosses)

Ch36 'The Scientific Giant Who Changed the World / 改变世界的科学巨匠' does not even hint at its actual topic: Einstein's Nobel being awarded for the photoelectric effect, not relativity.

suggested_fix: Vary the English title forms, keep 'World' to one or two uses, and align ch36 in both languages, e.g. '爱因斯坦的诺奖之路 / Einstein's Nobel, but Not for Relativity'. Apply the same cut to the Chinese '改变/重塑…世界' titles. The owner must sign off.

The ch36 opener question is '爱因斯坦因为什么获得诺贝尔奖？' while the title 'The Scientific Giant Who Changed the World' is generic. evidence: Plain colloquial titles ('会算术的马', 'OK 原本是个玩笑', '越狱的章鱼') sit next to stilted pseudo-classical ones: '稻济天下', '林下之网', '光之殇', '鲸歌易帜', '拥挤的苍穹', '拯救天空', '青蒿一握，济世千万'. Problem cases: '光之殇' (p7), where the article is about too much artificial light harming insects and the sky, so mourning 'the light' inverts the meaning; '鲸歌易帜' (p9), where 易帜 is a political term (change of flag/allegiance); '大恶臭逼出了下水道' (p8), which reads as 'forced out of the sewers'; '多莉：一只羊的复制' (p6), an awkward calque of 'copy' for 克隆; '一封信惊醒了达尔文' (p9), where 惊醒 means waking from sleep.
problem: The register swings between chatty and faux-literary 4-character formulas, and several titles carry the wrong connotation. The 'X之殇' and '…济天下' patterns are typical of generated headlines.
suggested_fix: Limit the fix to the real misfires: 34 '多莉：第一只克隆羊', 61 '座头鲸换了一首歌' (or '鲸歌的更替'), 55 '一场大恶臭，催生了伦敦下水道'. Optionally make 48 more concrete (e.g. '被灯光困住的昆虫'). Keep 29 '青蒿一握，济世千万' and 65 as they are. Owner sign-off is needed.
verify_reason: The register mix is real, but several cited examples do not hold. '青蒿一握，济世千万' alludes to Ge Hong's《肘后备急方》'青蒿一握，以水二升渍，绞取汁', the line Tu Youyou famously cited. That is an apt allusion, not an AI tell. '惊醒' has a standard figurative sense (使猛然醒悟), so '一封信惊醒了达尔文' is fine. 'X之殇' reads as 'the tragedy of/caused by X', so '光之殇' is vague but does not invert the meaning. The valid points are '多莉：一只羊的复制' (the standard term is 克隆), '鲸歌易帜' (易帜 is a political flag-change term) and '大恶臭逼出了下水道' (can be misread as 'forced out of the sewers'). Low-medium.

evidence: '一场火山喷发，与《弗兰肯斯坦》的诞生相连；一家胶卷巨头的技术领先，没有换来顺利转型；一手被解说员视作失误的棋，却显出机器的新思路。70篇故事从科学、历史与日常疑问出发，将重点词汇放进事件的起因、转折和结果。读到出人意料的结局，也读懂这些故事用到的英语。'

suggested_fix: Rewrite as a short hook plus 3-4 concrete selling points. For example: '70篇真实故事 × 每篇约270词'; '英文原文·中文对照·词汇与表达·文章简述'; 'xxxx条词汇，紧扣原句语境'; '配套B站70期讲解视频，扫码即看'; plus '适合：考研英语一/二、四六级备考'. Avoid reusing preface phrases.
verify_reason: The p475 text matches the quote exactly. It is a semicolon triad of abstract clauses, repeats '起因、转折和结果' from the preface ('篇末简述再把事件的起因、转折和结果讲明白'), closes on the '读到…也读懂…' antithesis, and states no concrete selling point (audience, unit structure, word count, videos).

In "in earnest" the point is that people really did it, not that they did it 认真地. 反噬 means "turning on one's master", not public backlash. 领衔 is used for casts and petitions, not for leading the news. The summaries on p22 and p60 render these correctly, so translation and summary contradict each other.
suggested_fix: Use the proposed rewrites, with "这道光束每年只照射两到三周、每天约两小时，这是由太阳的高度角决定的" for p19, and harmonize 仰角/太阳高度角 at the same time.
verify_reason: "因为这是太阳的仰角" (p19) is a broken causal sentence. "党派政治在全国宣传了这些字母" uses 宣传 (publicize) for 'propagated' (spread). "认真地这样做了" misses 'in earnest' = for real, and the p60 summary itself says "真开始这样批注". "领衔了两大电视网的新闻快报" (p39) is an odd collocation, and the p42 summary says "成为电视新闻头条". 反噬 is the weakest item: modern Chinese uses it loosely for 'backfire', but 强烈反弹 is the standard rendering of backlash.

evidence: "当时培养皿原封不动的在培养箱里放了约五天。"

evidence: Verbs glossed with 了: raided 抢劫了, pondered 仔细思考了, quizzed 测试了, garnered 赢得了, crept 悄悄爬了出去, erected 搭建了起来, relaunched 重新上市了, computed 算出了, sharpened 磨砺了, embrace 采纳了 (text: "now embrace"). Adjectives with 的: undue 过分的, earnest 真心实意的. Adjectives glossed as nouns: microbial 微生物, zoological 动物, illiterate 文盲, computational 计算, neurological 神经, molecular 分子, genetic 基因, forensic 法医学. Wrong form: distorted (adj.) 扭曲了, considerably (adv.) 相当大, sheer (adj.) 完全, rarity (n.) 罕见, vindication (n.) 证明了……是正确的.

suggested_fix: Apply one gloss style: base-form verbs without 了; adjectives ending in 的 (双重的, 合乎逻辑的, 坦率的); adverbs ending in 地 where natural; nouns as nouns (rarity 罕见之事；稀有). Where useful, add the context sense after a semicolon.

The gloss form switches from one entry to the next: verbs with 了 or 起来, adjectives with and without 的, adjectives glossed as nouns (微生物, 动物, 计算, 法医学), adverbs as adjectives (considerably 相当大), nouns as clauses (vindication 证明了……是正确的). Other instances: binned 被扔掉 and glossed as 被注释为 (passive glosses for verbs), atop prep. 顶部 (a noun gloss).

evidence: backlash 反噬 (p40); divine 神之一手 (p72); versatile 用途广泛 (p27, said of wits/anatomy); rationale 逻辑 (p14); in earnest 认真地 (p59, context = for real); propagated 宣传了 (p58); fixture 固定装置 (p21); oblivious 不知 (p27); pleaded 承认 (p66, from "pleaded guilty"); magnifying adj. 放大 (p20, split from "magnifying glass"); amateurs 业余者 (p72)

evidence: pdffonts: English body and titles are LiberationSerif / LiberationSerif-Bold / -Italic (metric clones of Times New Roman). Folios and TOC numbers are LiberationSans (Arial clone). All Chinese, including the long translation text, is NotoSansSC (embedded as "Noto Sans SC Thin Regular", a full variable font, not subset). A non-embedded Type 1 "Helvetica" is referenced on every page. The chapter badge "01" is Liberation Serif Bold while the TOC "01" is Liberation Sans Bold.
problem: Times/Arial clones are what generated documents and office defaults look like, and they strongly give away an automated layout. Long Chinese body text in a sans face also reads like a slide or web page, not a book. The non-embedded Helvetica reference and the unsubset variable CJK font will be flagged in printer preflight (PDF/X), and the "Thin" variable instance may render at the wrong weight on some RIPs.
suggested_fix: Choose a real book pairing: an English text serif with true italics and small caps (e.g. Source Serif 4, Crimson Pro, Minion) and a CJK serif for body (Source Han Serif / 思源宋体), keeping sans only for headings and labels. Use one numeral font throughout. Export PDF/X-4 with all fonts embedded and subset, and remove the unused Helvetica resource.

All of it will fail a PDF/X preflight, and Times/Arial clones signal office-default output.

evidence: p18 "a permanent fixture was announced: horizontal aluminium fins"; p56 "Partisan politics propagated the letters nationwide", "excavated the neglected Boston provenance from archival newspapers"; p44 "the painting was reinstated in the Louvre", "the heist elevated one esteemed gem among many to the world's most renowned painting"; p30 "Colonies blossomed."; p38 "launching the concoction was a wager"
problem: These are thesaurus substitutions that a native editor would not write. "A permanent fixture" is an idiom for something that is always there; the intended phrase is "a permanent fix". "Reinstated" is used of people or rules, not of a painting going back on its wall. One does not excavate a provenance. Such collocations make the English read as vocabulary-stuffed generated text, and the glossary then teaches them as models (fixture = 固定装置).
suggested_fix: As proposed, but drop the 'Colonies blossomed' example and add 'a South Korean Go professional with 18 international titles' (p69).

'Colonies blossomed' is a normal metaphor for bacterial growth and should be dropped from the list. 'reinstated in the Louvre' is unusual but defensible. A stronger example the finding missed: 'a South Korean strategist with 18 international titles' (p69) for a Go player, which led to the 战略家 mistranslation in finding 14.

evidence: EN p50 "In 1907 the psychologist Oskar Pfungst tested the act systematically"; ZH p51 "1907年，心理学家奥斯卡·普丰斯特系统地检验了这场表演"
problem: Pfungst ran his experiments in autumn 1904, right after the September 1904 commission. Carl Stumpf's report of December 1904 already announced the cueing explanation. 1907 is the year Pfungst's book "Das Pferd des Herrn von Osten" was published. As written, three years pass between the commission and the test with no explanation, and the date is wrong.
suggested_fix: EN: "Later that year the psychologist Oskar Pfungst tested the act systematically…" (optionally add: "his book appeared in 1907"). ZH: "同年稍后，心理学家奥斯卡·普丰斯特系统地检验了这场表演……".
verify_reason: Web search: Pfungst's book reprints the commission report of 12 September 1904 and Stumpf's report of 9 December 1904 (Supplement IV). Stumpf's introduction calls the December report the result of the scientific investigation, and says the solution was found in the questioner's unintentional minimal movements. So Pfungst's tests were done in autumn 1904, and 1907 is the year the German book was published (English translation 1911). The 1907 date seems to come from popular summaries such as Wikipedia's 'formal investigation in 1907'. Sources: gutenberg.org/files/33936/33936-h/33936-h.htm (contents and Stumpf's introduction, seen in search snippets; the page itself was blocked by the network), en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oskar_Pfungst.

verify_reason: Extracting the 70 English titles: 21 match 'The X That…', 25 contain 'That', and 6 more use 'The Man/Doctor/Woman Who'. '…the World' endings appear 4 times (Remade, Shook, Changed ×2).

evidence: Each article ends on a neat ironic sentence: 'keeps a quieter ledger of radiation's cost' (22), 'would, decades later, barely doze off' (23), 'The outdated rules she sailed under had stayed afloat since 1894; it took her dead to discredit them' (25), 'The legend had left him conspicuously unharmed' (26), 'The essence of Ge Hong's line lay in the boiling it skipped' (29), 'two rescuers were mourned' (30). Vocabulary-stuffed, unidiomatic phrasing: 'urged him to keep it hushed', 'decorated Sasson with national laurels', 'Kodak's manpower had reached an apex', 'Technical staffers were appreciative of the camera', 'a cumbersome heavyweight of about eight pounds' (p188); 'The two investigators attentively noted the fluctuations in his state as the deprivation progressively deepened' (p155, adverb stacking); 'had fuelled the tale, giving it impetus' (p174, redundant); 'The hypothetical scenario gave gamers a fictional nightmare' (p142, redundant).
problem: The fixed closing twist and the thesaurus-like word swaps (made to fit target words into the text) give the English a synthetic, generated feel that experienced teachers will recognise.
suggested_fix: Vary the endings, so that not every article closes on a kicker, and replace the forced items with natural word combinations ('told him to keep it quiet', 'awarded Sasson the National Medal of Technology', 'Kodak's workforce peaked at about 145,000'). Move the target word to a sentence where it is natural.
verify_reason: These closing kickers exist: ch22 'quieter ledger', 23 'barely doze off', 25 'it took her dead to discredit them', 26 'conspicuously unharmed', 29 'the boiling it skipped', 30 'two rescuers were mourned'. The phrases 'keep it hushed' (the idiom is hush-hush/quiet), 'decorated Sasson with national laurels', 'manpower had reached an apex', 'fuelled the tale, giving it impetus' and 'hypothetical scenario… fictional nightmare' are forced or redundant.

evidence: 'In November 2009 President Obama had decorated Sasson with national laurels… That medal's year also saw Kodak announce the end of Kodachrome.' (p188); translation '2009年11月，奥巴马总统授予萨松国家级荣誉' (p189); summary '2009年，萨松因数码相机获美国国家荣誉' (p192).
problem: Sasson is listed as a 2009 laureate of the National Medal of Technology and Innovation, but as far as I recall the White House ceremony where Obama presented the 2009 medals was on 17 November 2010. 'November 2009' therefore appears to mix up the medal's nominal year with the ceremony date. Please check against the White House/USPTO laureate list before printing.
suggested_fix: EN: 'In November 2010 President Obama presented Sasson with the National Medal of Technology and Innovation for 2009, commending his digital camera. That was the year Kodak had announced the end of Kodachrome.' ZH: '2010年11月，奥巴马总统向萨松颁发2009年度美国国家技术与创新奖章，表彰他发明数码相机；而正是在2009年，柯达宣布停产Kodachrome。' The summary p192 '2009年…获美国国家荣誉' can stay if it is changed to '获评2009年度…奖章'.
verify_reason: Web check: White House and AP coverage date the East Room ceremony where Obama presented Sasson the National Medal of Technology and Innovation to 17 November 2010; Sasson was in the 2009 laureate class (USPTO '2009 Laureates'; obamawhitehouse.archives.gov 2010/11/18; phys.org 'Obama rewards digital camera, microprocessor inventors', Nov 2010). Sasson's Wikipedia page has a '2009' typo, which is probably where the book's date came from. The Chinese '那枚奖章颁发的同年，柯达也宣布了Kodachrome的终结' (p189) is also wrong, because the medal was presented in 2010.

evidence: Summary: '真菌破坏控制咬合的肌肉，使下颚无法松开' (p146); the translation uses '双颚/颚部' (p143).
problem: In Chinese entomology an ant's biting mandibles are 上颚. 下颚 is the maxilla. The summary names the wrong mouthpart and also disagrees with the translation.
suggested_fix: '使双颚（上颚）无法松开'. It needs the owner's sign-off because it changes the approved video 简述.
verify_reason: In Chinese insect anatomy the mandible is 上颚 (大颚) and the maxilla is 下颚 (小颚), so the p146 summary '使下颚无法松开' names the wrong part and disagrees with the translation's 双颚/颚部. This summary is the owner-approved video 简述 (found verbatim in 14-actual-working-manuscript.md), so touches_user_approved_wording should be true.

evidence: The translations use thousands separators: '1,500', '10,000吨', '46,000吨', '1,178人', '2,200人' (p169); '1,100项' (p189); '45,000名居民' (p149); '2,000多个' (p195); '2,000名士兵' (p202). The summaries write '1500', '1178', '2200' (p172) and '1100项' (p192). The same texts also use 万 forms: '约1万人', '14.5万人', '4.7万个岗位'. Spacing is inconsistent: '了Kodachrome 的终结' vs '停产Kodachrome这种' (p189).
problem: Number style changes between the translation and the summary of the same chapter, and within the same page.
suggested_fix: Adopt one Chinese style (e.g. GB/T 15835: no comma in 4-digit numbers, 万 for large round numbers, '1500多人', '4.5万居民') and apply it everywhere. Normalise CJK–Latin spacing.
verify_reason: p169 '1,500/10,000吨/1,178人/2,200人' vs p172 '1500/1178/2200'; p189 '1,100项' vs p192 '1100项'; 万 forms elsewhere ('14.5万人', '4.7万个岗位', '1万个黑白像素'); p189 '了Kodachrome 的终结' has a stray space while '停产Kodachrome这种' has none.

evidence: Mistranslated technical terms: 'waterfront employment' → '纽约海滨区的就业人数' (p162; it means dock/longshore jobs, i.e. 码头就业; the summary p166 then says '滨水区'); 'corner fittings' → '角配件' (p162; the standard term is 角件); 'camera traps' → '相机陷阱' (p149; usual term 红外相机); 'carved into the rock' → '雕刻在岩石上面的阶梯' (p175; the steps were cut into the rock, 凿入岩体, not engraved on it). Terms change within a chapter: 公车/公共汽车/巴士 (p182); 无线电操作员 (p169) vs 报务员 (p172); 寄生虫 (p195) vs 疟原虫 (p199); 耐药性 vs 抗药性; 钢瓶 (p202) vs 气瓶 (p206); '约1万人' vs '约万人' (p206).
problem: Technical terms are rendered literally, and terminology shifts within one chapter. Attentive readers and teachers will notice.
suggested_fix: Use 码头就业（人数）, 角件, 在岩体中凿出的台阶, and one term each for bus and cylinder (公共汽车, 气瓶). 红外相机 is preferred but optional. Leave 寄生虫/疟原虫 as is.
verify_reason: These are confirmed: 海滨区 (p162) vs 滨水区 (p166) for dock employment; 角配件 instead of the standard 角件; '雕刻在岩石上面的阶梯' for steps cut into the rock; 公车/公共汽车/巴士 all on p182; 钢瓶 (p202) vs 气瓶 (p206). Two points are weaker: '相机陷阱' is attested in Chinese ecology papers (红外相机陷阱), and 寄生虫 (translation) vs 疟原虫 (summary) is a more specific term, not an inconsistency. Medium severity holds.

evidence: At 300 dpi the ant on p141 has four long legs gripping the vein. The left-most leg grows from the waist (petiole) next to the gaster, a looped limb runs from thorax to head, and only short stubs are under the thorax.
problem: This is a typical AI anatomy error. Insect legs attach to the thorax, and the image shows misplaced and extra limbs. A biology teacher would spot it in the chapter about ant anatomy and muscles.
suggested_fix: Regenerate or retouch: six legs from the thorax, mandibles clamped on the vein (the article's 'death grip'), and ideally a slightly lifeless pose.
verify_reason: A 200-dpi crop of p141 shows four long legs on the vein, with the left-most rooted at the petiole next to the gaster, a looped limb from thorax to head, and two short stubs under the thorax. The leg count and attachment points are anatomically wrong in a chapter about ant muscles.

evidence: p154 shows the supervising researcher (William Dement) as a grey-haired man of about 50; Dement was 35 in 1964. p193 shows Tu Youyou as a woman of about 60; she was 39–42 during the 1969–72 work described. The 'classical text' on the table is a thread-bound book with completely blank pages.
problem: These age anachronisms, plus the blank book (a common AI shortcut to avoid drawing text), weaken the illustrations' credibility for readers who know these well-known figures.
suggested_fix: Regenerate p193 with Tu at about 40 and a book with visible vertical text columns. Optionally make the p154 adult look mid-30s, but that is a minor point.
verify_reason: p193 shows Tu Youyou at about 60+ with glasses for the 1969–72 work, when she was 39–42, and the thread-bound book has completely blank pages. The p154 part is weaker: the grey-haired man is not identified, and he could be read as Ross rather than Dement, so it should not carry the finding.

evidence: p200: sunlit, clear turquoise water at a jungle-framed entrance, while the article stresses flooded, 'treacherous' passages (the real water was muddy with near-zero visibility). p179: the church through the bus window, yellow with red domes and twin towers, resembles Granada's cathedral rather than anything in Managua. p173: Carter peers through the hole by an oil lantern in open daylight, whereas the 26 November opening was at the end of an underground corridor by candlelight.
problem: Small details contradict the articles. They do not stand out on their own, but they add to a generic stock-image feel.
suggested_fix: When regenerating, put details from the article in the prompt: murky flood water and a narrow passage; a Managua street; a dark corridor and a candle.
verify_reason: p200 shows sunlit, clear turquoise water at the cave mouth (the real rescue had zero-visibility muddy water). The p179 yellow church with red domes and twin towers looks like Granada's cathedral rather than Managua's. p173 shows a lantern at a doorway open to daylight at the top of the stairs, whereas the 26 November breach was at the end of the descending corridor and Carter used a candle. Low severity is right.

evidence: English title capitalisation: 'The Fungus That Turns Ants into Zombies' (21) has lowercase 'into', but 'Eleven Days Without Sleep' (23) capitalises 'Without'. Elsewhere in the book: 'The Bread Made from Air' (45) vs 'The Truth About One Marshmallow' (18), 'Shadows of Wolves Over Yellowstone' (32).
problem: The title-case rule for prepositions is applied inconsistently in the table of contents and on the openers.
suggested_fix: Pick one rule and apply it to all 70 titles. Chicago (lowercase all prepositions): Without→without, About→about, Over→over, Beneath→beneath. AP (capitalise 4+ letters): into→Into, from→From.
verify_reason: The inconsistency is real, but the cited pair is not the best example: 'into'(4) lowercase vs 'Without'(7) capitalised fits a 5-letters-and-up rule. The true clash is between 4-letter prepositions: 'Over' (Shadows of Wolves Over Yellowstone) is capitalised, while 'into' and 'from' (Made from Air) are lowercase.

evidence: EN p161: 'In 1956 loading loose cargo cost about $5.83 a ton; loading the Ideal X cost, by the company's reckoning, about 16 cents.' ZH p162: '装载散货每吨花费约5.83美元；据公司估算，装载理想X号花费约16美分。' Summary p166: '该船每吨装船费约0.16美元'.

suggested_fix: ZH: '据公司估算，理想X号每吨装船费仅约16美分。' Optionally make the English explicit: 'about 16 cents a ton'.

evidence: Opener pages p141, 147, 154, 160, 167, 173, 179, 187, 193, 200 carry the running head '考研学人' at top left and the footer '21  让蚂蚁变僵尸的真菌 … 141' directly under a page that already shows the chapter number badge and the display title.
problem: Designed books drop running heads (and usually the title footer) on chapter-opening pages. Repeating the chapter title in small type under the same title in display type looks like a template applied to every page.
suggested_fix: Suppress the running head and footer title on opener pages (keep at most a folio, or none), as is conventional for chapter openers.

evidence: p247 '英文原文（续）' carries only two lines: 'A haven built against the apocalypse had a weakness at its own entrance, and warmer weather found it.' The other ~80% of the page is blank. The previous page (p246) ends at 84% of page height, while other chapters' English pages run to 89-90% (p240, p268).

suggested_fix: Pull the closing sentence back onto p246: trim paragraph spacing or leading on that page by 1-2 pt, or let the text block run a few mm deeper. Add a pagination rule that a continuation page must hold at least ~6 lines; otherwise tighten the previous page.
verify_reason: I opened p246 and p247. Text on p246 stops at about 83% of the page height. p247 holds only the two-line closing sentence under '英文原文（续）' and is otherwise blank. Pulling two lines back onto p246 is clearly possible, because p268 runs to about 89%.

evidence: p260 ends at 75% of page height, leaving ~6 empty lines. The whole next paragraph is pushed to p261 ('英文原文（续）'), which holds only 7 lines ('Byron's challenge proved fruitful ... and a teenager the monster.') and is two-thirds blank.

suggested_fix: Allow paragraphs to split across pages (with 2-line widow/orphan control), or fit long articles on one page by slightly reducing leading for that article. pp. 240 and 268 already fill 89-90%. Failing that, trim ~20 words with the owner's approval.

evidence: English p246: 'a homecoming began in 2017 ... That same year brought a scare. After record-breaking warmth, meltwater ran into the roughly 100-metre entrance tunnel'. Chinese p248: '同一年还有过一场虚惊'. The chapter's own summary p252 says: '虚惊：2017年报道的入口进水，实际发生于2016年10月异常温暖、多雨的天气后'.
problem: The water intrusion happened in October 2016 after record late-2016 warmth; it was only reported in May 2017. The article places the event in 2017, and the book's own summary contradicts it.
suggested_fix: Minimal edit (needs owner sign-off): 'News of a scare broke that year: in October 2016, after record-breaking warmth, meltwater had run into the roughly 100-metre entrance tunnel and frozen.' Chinese: '同年传出一场虚惊：2016年10月，一段破纪录的温暖天气过后，融水曾流进……'. Severity could be medium rather than high, but the contradiction with the summary is visible.
verify_reason: A web search confirms the meltwater entered the entrance tunnel in October 2016 after record autumn warmth. Statsbygg and the Norwegian government only disclosed it on 19-20 May 2017 (Guardian, Engadget, RNZ, Arctic Today). The English 'That same year [2017] brought a scare. After record-breaking warmth, meltwater ran into…' therefore misdates the event, and the book's own summary on p252 says it happened in October 2016.

evidence: In every 中文译文 page (pp. 209, 215, 221, 228, 234, 241, 248, 255, 262, 269), the Chinese equivalents of the bold English words are marked only by color. Sampled at 200 dpi on p215: body text ≈ rgb(40,56,48), highlighted words such as '标志性的' and '赶尽杀绝' ≈ rgb(40,72,64). pdffonts shows the only CJK font embedded is 'NotoSansSC-Thin' (one weight), so no real bold Chinese exists. At the 100-dpi proof the highlighting cannot be seen at all.
problem: The core bilingual feature (matching each bold English item to its Chinese equivalent) is effectively invisible in print. Readers will see an English page full of bold words next to a plain Chinese page.
suggested_fix: Embed a bold CJK weight (Noto Sans/Serif SC Bold or a 书宋/黑体 bold) and set the equivalents in true bold, in the same green as the English bold, or underline them. Then check the contrast on a printed proof.
verify_reason: I rendered p215 and p214 at 200 dpi and counted pixels. Chinese body text is rgb(41,59,53) and the highlighted equivalents (标志性的, 赶尽杀绝, 捕获…) are rgb(40,78,67). The English bold uses the same (40,78,67) but also bold weight. pdffonts shows a single CJK face (NotoSansSC-Thin), so the Chinese pairing relies on a very small colour shift that is invisible at 100 dpi and weak in print.

evidence: Unresolved 'A/B' alternatives remain in the running translation: p209 '这个离奇的意外纯属编造/虚构', '壁画的劣化/恶化变得显而易见'; p221 '任天堂抢得/抢下了掌机版权', '成立/创办了俄罗斯方块公司'; p255 '价格一路飙升/猛涨', '论述大众错觉/群体性妄想的书'; p262 '一场持续的/无休止的倾盆大雨', '科幻体裁/类型的开山之作'; p269 '一场十分激烈的争执/交锋'. A grep of all 中文译文 sections finds 108 such slashes in 44 chapters.

suggested_fix: Pick one rendering each time (e.g. 纯属虚构, 恶化, 拿下了, 创办了, 飙升, 群体性妄想, 无休止的, 科幻类型, 交锋). Run a global search for '[汉字]/[汉字]' in all translations and vocabulary glosses.
verify_reason: The quotes are accurate (p209 编造/虚构, 劣化/恶化; p221 抢得/抢下了, 成立/创办了; p255; p262; p269). My regex over the 中文译文 sections found about 101 Han/Han slashes in 43 chapters, close to the reviewer's 108/44. A grep of the repo shows the slashes come from the approved video scripts, so the fix does need owner sign-off (flag already set).

evidence: Seven of the ten articles share the same 'popular belief → debunk' turn: 'That fanciful mishap is a fabrication.' (31), 'Yet the census undermined the thinning claim' (32), 'Dolly is popularly called the first clone, a misconception.' (34), 'The analogy is intuitive but deceptive.' (35), 'Yet the archives tell a smaller story.' (38), 'Apple's garage origins are largely symbolic' (40), plus the Nobel/relativity twist (36). All ten end on a balanced, ironic one-line kicker: 'A tropical volcano had supplied the rain, and a teenager the monster.' / 'A haven built against the apocalypse had a weakness at its own entrance, and warmer weather found it.' / 'carried there by the man the prize had honoured.' / 'at the helm of the company that ousted him.' / 'later helped decide who could sell it.' / 'may deserve more trust than the fable ever did.'
problem: Read in sequence, the identical arc and the formulaic chiasmus closer form a recognisable LLM essay template. This is exactly the 'easy to recognise as AI' impression the owner describes.
suggested_fix: Same direction, but count it as 8 of 10 closers. Prioritise rewriting the kickers of ch33, 36, 37, 39 and 40, and leave the ch31 and ch34 endings.
verify_reason: The debunk arc and the balanced ironic closers are real and quoted correctly. However, 'all ten end on a kicker' is overstated: ch31 and ch34 end on plain descriptive sentences, so 8 of 10 do. The template effect is still clear when the chapters are read in sequence.

evidence: The prose is padded with synonyms so that target words fit in: ch31 'was on a woodland stroll ... with Robot, his canine companion', 'for an adventurous excursion, and the four explorers climbed down into the darkness', 'Ravidat embroidered his anecdote with a dramatic twist', 'That fanciful mishap is a fabrication', 'the pivotal initiative was the boys' own', 'Admirers now meet the bulls only in a recreation'; ch33 'grew engrossed in a diversion he had built', 'a chaotic muddle of overlapping deals', 'reaped none of the spoils', 'his arrangement's expiry'; ch39 'The melancholy weather was attributable to a distant blast', 'Mary began the ghastly yarn', 'Byron's poetic output included Darkness'; ch37 'cartons of precious seed sit silently'; ch40 'Exile proved productive.' The English pages have 54-71 bold items per ~270 words (ch33: 71).
problem: This elegant variation (stroll/excursion, anecdote/mishap/fabrication) and the stacked rare adjectives read as vocabulary-quota writing rather than journalism. A teacher will recognise the style as machine-generated, and some phrases are unidiomatic ('canine companion' for a named pet dog, 'poetic output included Darkness').
suggested_fix: Drop the 'canine companion' criticism. Cutting bold items to 30-35 changes the video-derived vocabulary design and should be offered to the owner as an option, not presented as a required fix.
verify_reason: Bold counts per article are 54-71 (ch33: 71), and the quoted padding is accurate. One claim is wrong: 'canine companion' is a common journalistic idiom, not unidiomatic. 'Byron's poetic output included Darkness' is the genuinely awkward phrase.

evidence: English appositives are copied as 'Name，一位/一个……，' in chapter after chapter: p221 '阿列克谢·帕基特诺夫，一位29岁的莫斯科程序员，', '罗伯特·斯坦因，一位富有进取心的英国软件商人，', '亨克·罗杰斯，一位足智多谋的荷兰裔发行商，', '斯坦因和凯文·马克斯韦尔，那位大亨的儿子，都在莫斯科'; p241 '阿尔瓦·古尔斯特兰德，一位获得过诺贝尔奖的眼科专家，'; p255 '查尔斯·麦凯，一位苏格兰记者，'; p248 'ICARDA，一个研究中心，它的基因库坐落于阿勒颇附近，'; p209 '拉斯科二号，一个精心制作的局部的复制品，'; p228 '她的名字，一个关于乳腺的双关语，致敬了多莉·帕顿'.
problem: This is the classic translationese marker. Native Chinese puts the description before the name ('29岁的莫斯科程序员帕基特诺夫'). Repeated across chapters, it makes the whole translation read as machine output.
suggested_fix: Recast as premodifiers or separate clauses, e.g. '1984年6月，29岁的莫斯科程序员帕基特诺夫迷上了自己编的一个小游戏。' / '苏格兰记者查尔斯·麦凯' / '研究机构ICARDA的基因库原在阿勒颇附近，叙利亚内战期间总部迁到了贝鲁特。'
verify_reason: I checked every quoted 'Name，一位/一个……，' appositive on pp. 209, 221, 228, 241, 248 and 255, and each is accurate. This is a recurring translationese pattern.

evidence: p221: '只有一块纯粹地文本的显示屏' (地 cannot modify a noun phrase); '所以每一个几何方块，由四个小格组成的，都是由字符拼装而成的' (an English relative clause dropped into the middle of the sentence); '这些版权在混乱的一团糟中，被持续地洗牌式地来回倒手，因为由西方公司之间重叠的交易而导致了这种情况' (因为…由…而导致 mixes two structures); '帕基特诺夫收获不到一点那些战利品（即收益），多年来始终如此'; '在前苏联，国家，而不是领工资的设计者，是这份知识产权的所有者' ('前苏联' is anachronistic for 1984).

It is a real meaning distortion, though medium is closer than high because it is not a full reversal.

evidence: EN: "That smoke, from coal burned in domestic fireplaces and power stations, was laden with soot and noxious sulphur dioxide." ZH: "这些煤烟来自于烧的煤，在家庭壁炉和发电厂里，充满了煤烟和有毒的二氧化硫。"

verify_reason: All the pairs check out. One example the finding missed: ch52 writes 约2万只 and 1万发 in the translation but 约两万只 and 一万发子弹 in the summary on p352.

evidence: Openings: 8 of 10 articles open with a precise date ("In 1936 the colossal Hindenburg…", "On 3 June 1952…", "In the fierce heat of summer 1858…", "J. Robert Oppenheimer, born in New York on 22 April 1904…", "In 1941…", "In the first ten days of September 1854…", "On 10 February 2009…", "On 18 February 1930…"). Endings: almost all close on an ironic one-line kicker — "A remedy aimed at the nose protected the gut." (ch55, set as its own paragraph), "The discoverer's ashes swept past the heart that bears his name." (ch60), "…exactly a year before the fire." (ch53), "…for fifty-five years beyond his lifetime." (ch56), "…stop using its own name for rivals' goods." (ch57), "…kept swerving around its splinters." (ch59), "…the atlas that steered the shearwater has yet to be read." (ch54). 7 of 10 use the 'X, not Y' antithesis ("seedlings, not elderly mothers", "swallowed, not inhaled", "inclination, not polarity", "an administrative proceeding, not a criminal prosecution", "where people died, not what they drank"…), and three paragraphs open with "Yet" (ch51, 55, 58).
problem: When chapters are read in a row, the same skeleton (date-stamped opening, chronological middle, antithesis, twist ending) becomes obvious. This uniform cadence is the main reason the English 'sounds AI'.
suggested_fix: Same fix, but with corrected counts: about 5/10 use the antithesis, and one paragraph opens with 'Yet'. The main lever is varying the date-stamped openings and the closing aphorism lines.

'X, not Y' (or 'not X but Y') appears in about 5 of the 10 articles (51, 52, 54, 56, 58), not 7. Only ch55 has a paragraph that opens with 'Yet'; in ch51 and ch58 'Yet' starts a sentence mid-paragraph. Medium severity stands.

evidence: Sentences bent to carry target words: "whose bombs were the collaborative creation of a thousands-strong workforce" (p375); "a presidential directive severed his access to confidential documentation" (p375); "62 survived, a proportion close to two-thirds, while a minority of 35 died" (p354); "This payout per bird gave farmers compensation and an incentive for extermination" (p348); "The first hints of a compass were celestial", "In 2014 came an eerie, man-made twist" (p361); "One owner's discarded relic demolished another's working asset", "The wreckage, however, endangered everyone else" (p395); "Amid the controversy, an irony was already in transit" (p402); "The underdog proved its utility in outer space" (p383).
problem: Abstract nouns and Latinate synonyms are stacked so that more key words fit into a sentence, giving an inflated register that no editor or native writer would choose. This is a recognisable LLM 'vocabulary-showcase' style.
suggested_fix: With owner sign-off, simplify where the key word is not essential (e.g. 'built by thousands of workers'; '62 of the 97 survived; 35 died'; 'Then, in 2014, came a strange twist'), or keep the key word but in a natural collocation.
verify_reason: All ten quoted sentences appear verbatim on p348, 354, 361, 375, 383, 395 and 402. The vocabulary-showcase register is real.

evidence: 9 of 10 guiding questions use the same two-clause frame '[topic phrase]，[怎样/为何/为什么/哪些]…？': 树木的地下联系，哪些已有证据？ / 一场被拍下的大火，怎样终结了飞艇客运时代？ / 能辨方向的鸟，怎样知道… / 下水道本为消除臭味，为什么还能减少疾病？ / 造出原子弹的科学家，为何被撤销涉密资格？ / 衣服上的刺果，怎样变成了日常搭扣？ / 破解霍乱之谜，关键是地图还是饮水？ / 两颗卫星相撞，为什么多年后仍要避让？ / 冥王星本身没变，为什么会失去行星身份？ Ch55 and ch60 share the further sub-template '本为/本身没变…，为什么…'. Book-wide, most of the 70 questions follow the same frame.
problem: Identical sentence architecture on every opener page reads as template output, not editorial voice.
suggested_fix: Vary the forms: a direct yes/no question (鸸鹋真的打赢了一场战争吗？), a quotation, a counter-intuitive statement followed by a question, a 'guess the number' prompt (这场大火烧了多少秒？), or a question addressed to the reader (如果你是1854年的医生…).
verify_reason: 9 of the 10 questions use the '[topic]，[wh-word]…？' frame; ch52 is the exception. A regex over all 70 dossiers matches the frame in 44 questions, which supports 'most'.

evidence: Every summary has exactly 5 bullets, each opening with a two-character label and a full-width colon. The arcs repeat: 发现/想象/复核/疑点/未定 (51); 困境/出兵/受挫/撤军/转向 (52); 隐患/失事/伤亡/原因/落幕 (53); 归巢/辨向/猜想/干扰/未解 (54); 危机/行动/工程/误判/结果 (55); 发现/重审/改类/争议/探访 (60). '发现' opens ch51 and ch60 (9 times book-wide), and 未定/未解 close ch51 and ch54. Ch51 label '想象' heads a bullet whose first sentence is fact (真菌能为植物找水和养分…), and '发现：1997年，实验发现…' echoes the label.
problem: A rigid 5×2-character scheme across 70 chapters is a strong mechanical signal, and some labels no longer fit their content.
suggested_fix: Let the number of points vary (3-6), drop or vary the labels (questions, key-sentence quotes, a timeline for history chapters, 'myth vs evidence' for science chapters), and fix mismatches (ch51 想象 → 走红 / 故事化).
verify_reason: The label arcs are quoted correctly. A book-wide tally confirms 发现 is used as a label 9 times. In ch51 the 想象 bullet opens with a factual sentence, and 发现：…实验发现 repeats the label. Ch57's 应用 bullet also opens with public rejection rather than an application.

evidence: Title: "原子弹之父的审判" / "The Trial of the Father of the Atomic Bomb". Article (p375): "…a security hearing, an administrative proceeding, not a criminal prosecution"; summary (p381): "这是行政审查，并非刑事起诉".
problem: The title calls it a trial while the text stresses that it was not one. An attentive teacher will spot the contradiction. The English title is also clumsy ("The Trial of the Father of the…").
suggested_fix: Lowest-cost option: put the word in quotation marks (原子弹之父的“审判”), or retitle (奥本海默安全听证案 / The Oppenheimer Hearing). This needs the owner's approval.
verify_reason: The contradiction between the title's 审判/Trial and p375 ('not a criminal prosecution') and summary p381 is real. 'Trial' is common figurative usage for this case, though, so the severity should be low, not medium.

evidence: The English appositive 'Name, a [role],' is copied into Chinese as '人名，一位X，' in several chapters: p384 "乔治·德·梅斯特拉尔，一位瑞士的工程师，…，一只爱尔兰的指示犬，"; p390 "约翰·斯诺，一位内科医生，自1849年起…" and "埃德蒙·帕克斯，一位临床医学教授，看到…"; p403 "把“plutoed”，这个戏谑的俚语，意思是“贬低”，评为…". Further calques: p397 "这是首次有意外相撞发生在两颗完整卫星之间", "这些残骸却危及了所有其他人", "国际空间站点火了它的推进器"; p403 "这个竞争者造成了一个尴尬的两难困境", "一个精确的定义便成了必需", "一件颇具讽刺意味的事早已在途中"; p362 "受骗的鸟儿随之转动以与之匹配", "它们找回了它们的方向", "事情出现了一个诡异的、人为的转折".
problem: These are standard translationese markers (apposition, possessive pronoun repetition, 'a + adj + noun' with 一个, 'X became a necessity'). Even where meaning is right, they make the Chinese read as machine output.
suggested_fix: Fold appositives into pre-modifiers (瑞士工程师梅斯特拉尔; 内科医生约翰·斯诺; 临床医学教授帕克斯), and recast: 两颗完整卫星首次意外相撞; 碎片却殃及所有其他航天器; 空间站启动推进器避让; 这颗竞争者让天文学界左右为难; 亟需一个精确定义; 一个讽刺早已在路上; 鸟儿随之转向; 又找准了方向.
verify_reason: All the quotes are verbatim on p384, 390, 397, 403 and 362. This overlaps with findings 2, 3, 5 and 7 and should be merged with them, but the cross-chapter apposition pattern is real.

evidence: EN: "The first hints of a compass were celestial." — ZH: "关于这种罗盘的最初迹象，是和天体有关的。"
problem: '这种罗盘' points back to a compass that has not been mentioned; the English introduces the idea with 'a'. The sentence also over-renders 'celestial' as 是和天体有关的.
suggested_fix: 鸟类体内有“罗盘”，最早的线索来自天空. Gloss celestial adj. 天体的；天空的.
verify_reason: On p362, 这种罗盘 has no antecedent, and the gloss "celestial adj. 和天体有关的" on p363 is clumsy. Low severity is right.

evidence: Summary bullets end with a one-character line: p387 "…1955年获得美国专" / "利。" and "…逐渐成为日常用" / "品。"; p406 "…太阳系第九颗行" / "星。". Also p381 "…裁定也未认定他" / "不忠。".
problem: A single character (plus full stop) alone on a line, often splitting a two-character word, is a visible widow that hand-set Chinese books avoid.
suggested_fix: Apply a widow rule (at least 3-4 characters on the last line) by adjusting tracking, or edit the bullet wording slightly.
verify_reason: The images show the single-character lines: p387 利。 and 品。, p406 星。, p381 不忠。. Polish-level, so low severity.

evidence: "相撞：2009年，两颗完整卫星首次意外相撞：失效的宇宙2251号撞上仍工作的铱星33号。"

evidence: Spacing between CJK and Latin/digits is inconsistent: title and footer "兴登堡号的 34 秒" and p384 "Velcro 这个名字…，velours 意为…" (with spaces) vs body "约7点25分", "1937年5月6日" and summary p387 "Velcro是品牌名" (no space). The title's 34 seconds also appears nowhere in the article, which says "about half a minute" (p354), as does the summary ("约半分钟").

suggested_fix: Pick one convention (e.g. no spaces, or a thin space set by the typesetter automatically) and apply it everywhere. Either mention the 34 seconds in the article or summary, or retitle (兴登堡号的最后航程).

The article (p354) and summary (p359) say only 'about half a minute'/约半分钟, never 34 seconds. The English title 'The Last Flight of the Hindenburg' does not match the Chinese title either.

evidence: The opener shows the damaged satellite against a pale blue, cloudy sky-wash, as if in the atmosphere; the article sets the collision 'nearly 790 kilometres above Siberia'. The ch60 opener (p401) likewise puts New Horizons and Pluto against a grey-green wash.
problem: In orbit the background is black. A science-literate reader will notice the satellite appearing to float in daytime sky, an artifact of the image model's watercolour style overriding physics.
suggested_fix: Regenerate or retouch with a dark (black or indigo) space background while keeping the watercolour paper border, for consistency with the series style.
verify_reason: The ch59 opener on p394 does use a pale blue, cloud-like wash, but Earth's curved limb is drawn below, so the orbital setting is clear. The ch60 opener on p401 uses a darker grey-green. The light background follows the book-wide watercolour-on-parchment style rather than being a clear AI artifact. Defensible either way, and very low priority.

evidence: The opener shows a gas case with a clear hose that coils on the ground and connects to nothing; the tied bags over the birch and fir seedlings have no inlet.

suggested_fix: Retouch so the hose runs into the bag over one seedling, or remove the case.
verify_reason: A 4x crop of p340 shows the clear hose leaving the case fitting and lying coiled on the ground, connected to neither bag. The tied bags have no inlet. Low severity is right.

evidence: Ch55 (Great Stink, p368: "The predominant belief, miasma, blamed disease on foul air") and ch58 (Snow and Broad Street, p389: "Most doctors attributed epidemics to miasma, foul air arising from filth") cover the same 1850s London miasma/cholera story three chapters apart, with no cross-reference, and gloss the same words again (foul air / foul 污浊的).

suggested_fix: Add a one-line cross-reference box (参见第58篇：斯诺与宽街水泵 / 参见第55篇：大恶臭) and let ch58's vocabulary skip, or point back to, the words already taught in ch55.

evidence: p375 "a **presidential directive severed** his **access to confidential documentation**" is printed as two unbroken bold runs, but it is six separate glossary entries (presidential adj., directive n., severed v., access to n., confidential adj., documentation n., p379). Similar runs: p389 "**inquiry declined to condemn**"; p361 "**posted a letter at once**", "**feathered traveller**"; p395 "**discarded relic demolished**", "**Space Station fired**", "**impact flung out**". In split phrases the particle is bolded onto the wrong word: p348 "**toughness to** the armour" (the entry is 'likened to'), p341 "**seedlings in** them" (the entry is 'enclosed in'), p368 "denounced the river **as**", p361 "**piping** radio noise **in**".
problem: Bold plus green is the only marker, so a student cannot see where one key item ends and the next begins. Fragments such as 'toughness to' and 'seedlings in' look like collocations, which teaches wrong chunks, and the English page does not map cleanly onto the glossary.
suggested_fix: Give each highlighted item a visible boundary, for example a per-item underline with gaps, two alternating tints, or small superscript numbers that match the glossary order. For discontinuous phrases (enclose…in, liken…to, denounce…as, pipe…in), mark both halves with the same index instead of bolding the particle as if it belonged to the neighbouring noun.

evidence: These instances are not covered by findings 17 or 19. p363 "duped v. 受骗的" (in 'The duped birds' the word is adjectival, and the gloss is adjectival under a v. tag); p364 "tuned adj. 调校" (adj. tag with a verb gloss) and "finely adv. 精细"; p363 "celestial adj. 和天体有关的"; p398 "constellation n. 星座" (the context is 'satellite-phone constellation'); p386 "aesthetic n. 审美".
problem: The tag and the gloss disagree, or the gloss gives the wrong sense: bare 星座 teaches the zodiac meaning, and 审美 means 'taste', not 'look'. Learners copy these into their own word lists.
suggested_fix: duped adj. 受骗的; finely tuned adj. 调校精细的 (or tune v. 调校; finely adv. 精细地); celestial adj. 天体的；天空的; constellation n. 星座；（卫星）星座/卫星群; aesthetic n. 美感；外观风格.

evidence: Within ch56, 'security clearance' is rendered three different ways: opener question p374 "为何被撤销涉密资格？"; translation p377 "恢复安全许可", "撤销安全许可带来的污名" and gloss p380 "clearance n. 安全许可"; summary p381 "拒绝恢复他接触机密资料的资格".

suggested_fix: Choose one term, e.g. 安全许可（涉密资格） at first mention and 安全许可 afterwards, and use it in the question, the translation and the summary.

evidence: EN: "Proposed in 2000, cryptochrome, a protein in the retina, is now the foremost suspect." ZH: "2000年被提出的隐花色素，是视网膜中的一种蛋白质，如今它是头号嫌疑对象。"
problem: The Chinese reads as if cryptochrome itself was first proposed, that is discovered, in 2000. The English means that in 2000 it was proposed as the bird's magnetic sensor (the 2000 radical-pair/cryptochrome hypothesis). Cryptochromes were already known in the 1990s.
suggested_fix: 2000年，有学者提出视网膜中的一种蛋白质隐花色素可能就是感磁元件；如今它是头号嫌疑对象。

evidence: On every 中文译文 page (p409, 416, 423, 430, 437, 443, 450, 456, 463, 470) the Chinese key equivalents, e.g. 雄性座头鲸, 繁殖地, 萦绕于心头的 (p409) and 强大的, 才智, 勾勒了 (p416), use the same font and weight as the body text (NotoSansSC, 12 pt). The only difference is colour: #284e43 against the body's #293b35. At 100 and 220 dpi they look almost the same as the surrounding text. The English key words use real bold.

suggested_fix: Embed a real heavier CJK weight (Noto Sans SC / Source Han Sans Medium or Bold, or Source Han Serif Bold if the body moves to a serif) and use it for the paired equivalents, or add a clear underline or accent colour. Then run pdffonts to check that the bold face is embedded.
verify_reason: Checked with PyMuPDF on p409. The 'bold' Chinese spans are NotoSansSC-Thin 12 pt in #284e43 and the body is the same font and size in #293b35. pdffonts lists no bold CJK face on p409. In a 250 dpi crop the key words are only a slightly greener tint with no weight difference, so the English-to-Chinese pairing can't be seen. This affects the whole book, not only 61-70.

evidence: Draft alternatives separated by slashes are printed inside the running translation. p409 每一次表演/演奏持续数分钟. p416 他被剥夺/丧失了他的安全许可. p430 has five: 一团零星的/散落的霉菌; 粗糙的/未加工的液体; 稀罕物/奇物; 锲而不舍的/坚持不懈的; 辛劳/辛苦工作. p443 这套计划/方案彻底失败. p456 has five more: 发动机/引擎; 转接器/转换插头; 被内置了/埋下了; 燃烧起来了/着火了; 巧思/足智多谋 (this last one is split across a line as 足智多/谋。). The same slash glosses appear in the vocabulary lists (p410 表演/演奏, p419 被剥夺/丧失了, p431 零星的/散落的, p445 计划/方案, p457-459 发动机/引擎 etc.).

suggested_fix: Keep the reviewer's single renderings in the translation (stray → 飘来的/偶然落入的). In the glosses, use the dictionary form with semicolons (表演；演奏, 计划；方案) or a single best gloss. Never use a slash.
verify_reason: Every slash pair quoted is in the dossier text and visible on the page images: p409 表演/演奏; p416 被剥夺/丧失了; p430 five pairs; p443 计划/方案; p456 five pairs, with 足智多/谋。 broken across the last line. The same pairs appear as glosses on p410, p419, p431, p433, p445, p458 and p459. For 'stray mould', 零星的/散落的 is also the wrong sense: the mould drifted in, it was not scattered. The proposed 飘来的 fixes that too.

evidence: The translation keeps English word order, leaving time phrases dangling at the end: 艾伦·图灵生于1912年6月，他已拥有强大的才智，二十出头时。 and 他死于氰化物中毒，1954年6月7日。 There is a doubled-的 bracket: 他团队（研制的）的机器. And a 的-chain: 他加入了布莱切利园的保密的破译工作，领导关于海军恩尼格玛密码机的工作，即德国的加密机器。
problem: These are word-for-word calques of English syntax that no Chinese editor would let through. 二十出头时 tacked on after the full stop reads as an error, and （研制的）的 is ungrammatical.
suggested_fix: For example: 艾伦·图灵生于1912年6月，二十出头便已才智过人。…… 1954年6月7日，他死于氰化物中毒。…… 他团队研制的机器…… 1939年9月4日，他加入布莱切利园的秘密破译工作，主攻德国海军的恩尼格玛加密机。
verify_reason: All quotes are exact on p416: 他已拥有强大的才智，二十出头时。 / 他死于氰化物中毒，1954年6月7日。 / 他团队（研制的）的机器 / 布莱切利园的保密的破译工作，领导关于海军恩尼格玛密码机的工作，即德国的加密机器. These are English-order calques. The proposed rewrites are idiomatic and keep the meaning.

evidence: 连续三年贫乏的降雨，从2015到2017年，减少了水库的蓄水，这些水库给一个大都市区供水，大约400万人口。 Also: 这个词指的是一道严酷的门槛：即当该市水库的存水按占水库容量的百分比降至13.5%时达到的门槛。 And 每人被分配每天50升水 / 城镇区，在种族隔离制度下按种族被隔离出来的贫困地区，长期以来……
